summary: Feed s163_triple to IDS is degraded: 6.6% TCP packet loss (high), 73.6% encrypted bytes exceeds 60% IDS tolerance, and 29.1% VXLAN-encapsulated traffic is not stripped. IDS requires full payload and both directions - drops and encapsulation cause missed detections, encryption blinds payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is dropping packets before the IDS - 210 of 3180 TCP packets show gaps/retransmissions (6.6% vs 1% threshold). Tool overload check is healthy, so loss is upstream of the tool, likely SPAN oversubscription or broker egress congestion/policing.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS misses TCP segments and cannot reassemble flows or match signatures; 6.6% loss causes severe false negatives and broken stream reassembly for this IDS that needs full payload and both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute load and reduce per-egress burst drops at the packet broker; if SPAN-sourced, replace SPAN with TAP and use broker load-balancing to keep loss <1% for reliable IDS detection.

findings.root_cause: 74% of bytes are TLS/encrypted vs 60% IDS tolerance. Traffic is predominantly encrypted and forwarded without broker-based decryption or selective forwarding to a decryption zone.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS that needs full payload is blind to 74% of bytes - cannot inspect encrypted payloads for exploits/malware/C2, sharply reducing detection coverage to metadata only.

recommended_fix.why: IDS cannot detect threats inside encrypted sessions without cleartext; decrypt once at visibility layer (or via dedicated TLS inspection) and forward cleartext to IDS, respecting privacy/policy.

findings.root_cause: 29.1% of frames (942/3238) arrive inside VXLAN encapsulation that the packet broker is not stripping. IDS sees outer VXLAN/IP/UDP headers only.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot parse inner L2-L7 headers or apply signatures to encapsulated traffic; VXLAN-hidden lateral movement, C2, and exploits are missed and correlation fails.

recommended_fix.why: Strip VXLAN at the packet broker to expose inner Ethernet/IP payload to IDS for full signature matching, while optionally forwarding outer headers as metadata.
